I am an old man now, 72 years, and I have farmed these lands in Mangochi all my life. On this small piece of 0.45 hectares I plant beans together with my maize and pigeon peas, the way my father taught me, because the beans help the soil and feed my family when the maize is finished. I have no money for the chemical fertilizer this year — the prices at the trading centre are too high for a man like me — but I put the manure from my few goats and chickens on the plot before the rains came. I keep the seed from last harvest, the local beans that I know grow well here near the lake, and my grandchildren and my wife help me weed and harvest, though my back is not what it was.
